run.question: In the elasticsearch index 'app-275-logs-qe7p2k4d', run a `term: { level: "ERROR" }` query and tell me how many hits come back. If that returns zero, find the right field for log level and re-run the query.

report.summary: The term query on field 'level' returned zero hits, because the index app-275-logs-qe7p2k4d has no 'level' field: its mapping contains only @timestamp (date), message (text), service (keyword) and severity (keyword). The log-level field is 'severity', and term { severity: "ERROR" } returned 10 hits inside the tool's applied window 2026-11-23T17:08:04Z to 2026-11-23T18:08:04Z. All 30 documents matching in that window belong to service checkout-275 and split as INFO 15, ERROR 10, WARN 5. The sampled ERROR documents are messages 'DB connection refused 1/2/3' from checkout-275 written at 18:04:01Z, 18:04:02Z and 18:04:03Z; the underlying DB entity is not identified in this evidence, so no root cause is named.

claims.text: The mapping of index app-275-logs-qe7p2k4d has exactly four fields: @timestamp (date), message (text), service (keyword), severity (keyword); there is no 'level' field in the mapping.

The query {"term":{"level":"ERROR"}} on index app-275-logs-qe7p2k4d returned total 0 hits (relation eq) with shards successful 1, failed 0, in the tool-applied @timestamp window 2026-11-23T17:08:04Z to 2026-11-23T18:08:04Z.
Re-running against the actual log-level field, {"term":{"severity":"ERROR"}}, returned total 10 hits (relation eq) in the same window 2026-11-23T17:08:04Z to 2026-11-23T18:08:04Z.

A terms aggregation on severity over the same index and window returned INFO 15, ERROR 10, WARN 5 with sum_other_doc_count 0 (total 30 documents), and the service terms aggregation returned a single bucket service=checkout-275 with 30 documents.
Aggregated by service, all 10 severity=ERROR documents in the window belong to service checkout-275 (single bucket, doc_count 10, sum_other_doc_count 0).

The three oldest severity=ERROR documents shown are service checkout-275 with messages 'DB connection refused 1' (@timestamp 2026-11-23T18:04:01Z), 'DB connection refused 2' (18:04:02Z) and 'DB connection refused 3' (18:04:03Z). A later attempt to use {"query":{"term":{"level":"ERROR"}}} as the whole request body was rejected by Elasticsearch with parsing_exception 'unknown query [query]' and returned no data; the corrected body form {"term":{"level":"ERROR"}} is the one that returned 0.

The 10 ERROR lines ('DB connection refused') suggest checkout-275 could not reach a database dependency around 2026-11-23T18:04Z; no database, endpoint or config object is identified in this evidence, so the cause of the refusals and any impact beyond checkout-275's own ERROR log lines remain unverified.

gaps: The counts cover only the tool-applied 1-hour window 2026-11-23T17:08:04Z to 2026-11-23T18:08:04Z; the matched documents themselves span only 18:04:01Z to 18:06:15Z (source_start_at/source_end_at), and no other time range or the wider authorized window was queried, so ERROR counts outside that hour are unknown.

Whether the index ever had a 'level' field, or whether ERROR text exists only inside the message field rather than a level field, was not verified; only the current mapping and current-window queries were checked.

The number of ERROR lines per exact timestamp beyond the 3 shown documents is not enumerated (10 matched, 3 shown), and the identity of the database or endpoint behind 'DB connection refused' is not observable in this index.
Kubernetes, Jaeger and Prometheus signals were not queried in this Run, so pod/deployment state, error spans and failure rates for checkout-275 are unknown.
